- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (positive sentiment > 0.5 → model tends to overshoot).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (sentiment < -0.5 → model underreacts).
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term sentiment volatility; smooth out sharp swings in forecast.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially after sentiment shifts.
- When sentiment is rising, model often overweights recent price momentum; reduce momentum bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates later periods (e.g., days 15–30) when sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to forecast higher than true outcome — apply downward bias.
- Avoid extrapolating sentiment trends beyond 3–5 days; sentiment decay reduces forecast accuracy after 10 days.
